# Deviations from `Paper6_Methodology_IEEE.docx`

Each entry gives what the methodology (or the task brief) says, what was done, and why. On 2026-10-12 the author delegated every open decision ("do your best recommendation … I am leaving all things on you"). All entries below are therefore **applied**. No method, index, period, threshold or test was changed beyond what is listed. Since v2.2 this file is generated by `scripts/15_render_deviations.R` from `DEVIATIONS.template.md`: every value that the current pipeline computes is a placeholder filled from `results_text/key_numbers.rds` (trace: `results_text/DEVIATIONS_trace.csv`). Values in columns headed *Old (v1)*, *New (v2)* or *Old (v2)* and the text of superseded rows quote the version named and are kept as a historical record; they are not regenerated.

Far-future Δ drought frequency SSP2-4.5 / SSP5-8.5: new 10 +10.0 / +11.1, old 10 +10.7 / +12.8, all 27 +8.3 / +9.9 %-points. | Ranking stability had not been tested. |
| F5 | FDR on projection maps (Item 5) | Cell robustness: ≥ 80% agreement and Wilcoxon p < 0.05 per cell | Benjamini–Hochberg across the cells of each map. Robust share of the regional cells, far future: 82.5% / 87.7% (without FDR 82.5% / 87.7%); mid-century SSP5-8.5 0.0% (without FDR 40.4%). | Many correlated cell tests. |

## v3 changes (2026-10-23): PMD station and WAPDA discharge records supplied by the author

PMD daily records (Islamabad, Murree; P, Tmax, Tmin, 1961–2010) and WAPDA/SWHP daily discharge (Soan at Dhok Pathan 1964–2003, Soan at Chirah 1962–2003, Sil River near Chahan 1962–2003) were added (`Real dataset/`, parsed by `scripts/05_read_pmd_wapda.R`). The whole analysis was rerun from an empty cache. Old values are from tag `v2.2-pre-realdata`; before/after headline numbers are in `CHANGES_v3.md`.

| # | Item | v2.2 | v3 (generated from key_numbers.rds) | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D4 (v3) | Station network (Table I) | GSOD/ISD and GHCN-D only; accepted for P + ET0: Chaklala, Jhelum, Peshawar Intl | PMD Islamabad merged into WMO 41577 (Islamabad City) and PMD Murree into WMO 41573; PMD values replace GSOD P, Tmax and Tmin. Accepted for P + ET0: Chaklala, Islamabad (PMD), Jhelum, Murree (PMD), Peshawar Intl | The methodology (II-B, Table I) specifies PMD stations; records were obtained from PMD for two of them. PMD Murree matches GSOD Murree day by day; PMD Islamabad agrees best with GSOD Islamabad City and only weakly with Chaklala (daily P r ≈ 0.35), so Chaklala stays separate. |
| D22 | Dew point and wind at the PMD stations | – | Murree: ERA5-Land at the station point quantile-mapped per calendar month to GSOD Murree, over the whole record (GSOD dew point observed on 27.7% of 1985–2014 days). Islamabad: gap-filled Chaklala dew point and wind (11 km, same 0.25° cell; GSOD Islamabad City has < 60 dew-point days per calendar month) | The PMD files contain no humidity, wind or sunshine; with the ≤ 15-day gap rule alone, PM ET₀ (and SPEI, RDI) would be undefined at both stations. Rs is estimated from the temperature range as for every station (FAO-56 Eq. 50). |

GloFAS kept as the 1981–2024 extension (k = 1, r = 0.50) and validated against the gauges: monthly KGE 0.59 (Dhok Pathan), 0.23 (Chirah); Table S7 | The methodology specifies WAPDA discharge at Chirah and Dhok Pathan. The gauge records end in 2003, so only 1985–2003 of the common baseline is covered; 1985 onwards also follows the Simly Dam (1983) upstream of Chirah. |

WAPDA: m³ s⁻¹ sheets used; 10-day "Mean" rows dropped; Sil 1962 (Jan–Apr) missing. ## v3.1 changes (2026-10-23): code-level fixes after the code audit of v3

| # | Item | v3 | v3.1 (generated from key_numbers.rds) | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Station KGE in the GCM ranking (III-E) | Mean over stations; Chaklala and Islamabad (PMD) share one 0.25° cell, so that cell counted twice | Mean over cells: the eligible stations of a cell are averaged first (`station_kge()`, `scripts/R/ranking_helpers.R`), in the full-sample evaluation and in every bootstrap replicate | Each grid cell must enter the point-to-grid comparison once. |
| C2 | Station representativeness (III-E, IV) | All accepted stations in the domain compared with their cell | Stations with \|elevation − cell mean\| > 500 m are not used for station-based evaluation (GCM station KGE, ET0 skill, station vs gridded indices); kept for the observed station series. Excluded: Murree (PMD) | A point 750 m above its cell mean measures the lapse-rate difference, not model skill. |
| C3 | Homogeneity (III-B) | Absolute SNHT and Pettitt; results reported but not used | Relative tests on station/reference ratios (P, ET0) or differences (Tmax, Tmin) against two independent references (CHIRPS/ERA5-Land at the station point; TerraClimate at the station cell); a series is suspect only if SNHT and Pettitt both reject against both references, and suspect series are not used in station-based evaluation. Suspect series: Chaklala ET0, Chaklala Tmax, Islamabad (PMD) ET0, Islamabad (PMD) Tmax, Jhelum P, Jhelum Tmax, Murree (PMD) ET0, Murree (PMD) Tmax, Peshawar Intl P, Peshawar Intl Tmax, Peshawar Intl Tmin | SNHT is a relative test (Alexandersson 1986); absolute tests confuse climate variability with inhomogeneity, and a detected inhomogeneity has to have a consequence. |
| C4 | ET0 at stations without observed humidity/wind | PM ET0 from ERA5-Land humidity and wind counted as complete | ET0 is evaluated only where ≥ 70% of 1985–2014 months have observed (or short-gap filled) humidity and wind; Table I column "Obs. humidity/wind". Not evaluated for ET0: Murree (PMD) | Comparing ERA5-Land ET0 with a station ET0 computed from ERA5-Land humidity and wind is circular. |
| C5 | Propagation (III-D) | SPEI of the Dhok Pathan basin for all three gauges | Each gauge with its own catchment SPEI: Dhok Pathan basin and the delineated Chirah catchment (353 km²); the Sil gauge (no location) is used for SRI/SDI only. Dhok Pathan: k = 1, lag 0, r = 0.61; Chirah (lag 0): k = 2, r = 0.51 | Meteorological and hydrological drought must refer to the same catchment. |
| C6 | Duration margin and ties in the copulas (III-F, Eq. 8) | D (whole months) fitted with continuous distributions (lognormal selected, rejected by the marginal tests); ties of the pseudo-observations broken at random, so Table S6 and Table V differed | D − 1 fitted by AIC among geometric, Poisson and negative binomial; S − 1 (S ≥ 1 by construction) with a semiparametric margin (empirical body, generalized Pareto tail above the 90th percentile) for the pooled sets (≥ 100 events), otherwise by AIC among exponential, gamma, Weibull and log-normal; pseudo-observations with mid-ranks (deterministic, independent of row order). Pooled sets passing the parametric-bootstrap AD test for D: 10 of 10; for S: 10 of 10 | Durations are counts; with a discrete margin the Item 2 continuity point F_D(k − 0.5) equals P(D < k) exactly. |
| C7 | Exposure uncertainty (III-F, IV) | Ensemble value only | Per-model exposure change, weighted 10th–90th percentile range and 1,000-replicate model-level bootstrap CI (Table S8). Far future, SSP5-8.5, all units: 70.8% (CI 38.8 to 104.2%) | The methodology (IV) asks for uncertainty to be reported with the results. |
| C8 | Effect of QDM on the drought signal (Item 3) | Precipitation inflation reported, drought-frequency effect only in Table VII | Model-by-model far-future Δ drought frequency without and with QDM: SSP2-4.5 +11.5 / +10.0, SSP5-8.5 +14.6 / +11.1 %-points. The primary QDM is kept, as pre-registered (Item 3: no switch after a failed criterion) | The failed acceptance criteria are reported together with their consequence. |
| C9 | Reporting and checks | Values rounded before the text generator (double rounding); number trace matched unsigned numbers; Table S3 note named the unadjusted test | Key numbers stored at full precision and rounded once when printed; number trace sign-sensitive; Table S3 note names the BH-adjusted test; unit tests for the PMD/WAPDA parsers, propagation, discrete margins, mid-rank ties and the per-cell station KGE (`tests/test_pmd_wapda.R`) | Code-audit findings. |
